episode_title: IoT Trojectory Podcast - Episode 19 - Interview with Esteban Rubens - Healthcare AI

real_qa.q: How does NetApp use AI in healthcare and what infrastructure challenges do data scientists face?
real_qa.r: NetApp enables the right infrastructure to make the job of data scientists easier by providing data management solutions. Deep learning in healthcare requires a lot of labeled data to train models. However, data scientists spend 75 to 90 percent of their time on data preparation, data cleansing, normalization, data movement, and data mining rather than actual data science work. This is often caused by not having the right infrastructure, such as data silos. NetApp works as one leg of a three-legged infrastructure stool alongside compute from NVIDIA and fast networking like 100 gigabit per second networking to solve these challenges.
real_qa.requete: NetApp healthcare AI infrastructure data scientists

real_qa.q: What are specific clinical applications of deep learning AI that NetApp enables in healthcare organizations?
real_qa.r: Early sepsis prediction is one major use case where deep learning models trained on EHR data including vital signs and medical history can warn clinical staff four to six hours before a patient will experience sepsis, allowing earlier intervention. Readmission prevention is another application where keeping patients in the hospital one or two days longer can reduce readmission risk significantly. Additionally, deep learning is being used to combat clinical burnout by streamlining data entry, avoiding repetition, and prioritizing alarms to reduce alert fatigue. Nuance's ambient computing technology uses natural language processing to transcribe clinical conversations without requiring clinicians to stare at screens.
real_qa.requete: deep learning sepsis prediction EHR clinical applications
